data.narrative:
Foundry Robotics, a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company led by Adarsh Kulkarni, has raised $19M to date. The valuation exercise draws from a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ), though the narrow peer set at identical stage limits full triangulation.

The Stage-Progression method, the only fully applicable approach, uses $19M in total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression. This yields an implied value of $48M. The Peer-Median method proved inapplicable: while ten robotics peers exist sector-wide, the filter for same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables yielded fewer than three datapoints, making a narrow median unreliable. An all-sector median would introduce undue noise given sector heterogeneity and was therefore excluded.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $40M (low) to $55M (high), with a median of $48M. This range reflects the step-up progression logic but carries material uncertainty around (1) the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for this specific sub-stage transition, and (2) the absence of sufficient peer benchmarks to validate or adjust the methodology. Further stage-specific data on comparable Seed→Series A outcomes in robotics would narrow this band materially.
